facts.premium: Isan's most industrial province; factory and logistics wages above the rural Isan norm but still below national.
facts.skill_gap: Manufacturing/logistics demand outpaces local skilled supply; many higher-skill roles filled by in-migrants.
anchors: Gateway manufacturing & logistics (~1,800 factories, ~112k factory workers) on the Bangkok–Isan corridor
Korat city — regional retail, university and healthcare hub
Pak Chong / Khao Yai tourism and agribusiness
workers: Farmers and farm labour (rice, cassava, sugarcane)
Factory and logistics workers around Korat & Sung Noen
Informal traders, market vendors and gig riders
Construction and service workers in Korat city
impacts: OAE shows fresh cassava down ~20-25% YoY; squeezes upcountry farmer cash flow and repayment.
Rain-fed rice and cane make harvest income weather-dependent; a poor monsoon hits repayment broadly.
Factory and logistics expansion adds the region's most stable wage base; supports pickup collateral.
Firmer sugar and hom-mali rice cushion farm income against cassava weakness — watch the swing.
Many households depend on transfers from migrant workers; downturns elsewhere reach Korat fast.
